source_checks.independence: Bromley acknowledges Collier, so these are not fully independent historiographical lineages. He independently examines Science Museum notations and reconstructs the 1838 design: his comparison of loom-type card strings and operation/variable strings adds technical evidence, although the original designers records and historical attribution ultimately remain Babbage-associated. He describes analysis as simplified and tentative, with less than 10% of material studied in detail.

claim_reviews.rationale: 1843 pp. 677–678 describe the engine and operation/variable cards; the 1878 committee section IV records only a partial mill built. Scope is a design and mechanical computing.

The catalogue dates Sketch 13 to 1837 and identifies a punched-card mechanism; image shows multiple dates and a perforated arrangement. This is the archive date for a multilayer drawing, not proof of the exact date when each component was added or priority over earlier designs. Existing caveat expresses multiple stages.

1843 publication and statement supported; Note E p. 720, PDF p. 55, specifically describes the Engine prism turning backwards to reuse cards. Revised citation correctly distinguishes Note C’s separate proposed loom mechanism.

Babbage’s 1839 attribution and Menabrea’s description establish the historical direction, with Collier’s separate notebook-based chronology and Bromley’s independent examination of design notations providing informative documentary and structural corroboration. Collier and Bromley are not wholly independent of Babbage or each other, but they add distinct archival and technical evidence beyond a copy of the 1839 statement. Bromley §12 p. 215 supports distinct operation and variable strings and the correspondence to loom strings. Removed to_event avoids falsely tying both functions to the 1837 sketch. The attribution does not settle Babbage’s first encounter or date of each component.
